smell: Execute() repeats the same `if err := X(...); err != nil { errs = append(errs, err) }` shape eight times for the Full cleanup case and once each for the *Only kinds. The cleanup pipeline is a fixed, declared list of named steps; iterating over a slice of (label, fn) pairs would shrink the body to ~10 LOC and make the kind→steps mapping data-driven.
fix_summary: Replace the switch with a `cleanupStep` struct ({label, fn func() error}) and a kind→[]cleanupStep map. A single loop calls each fn and accumulates errs. Drops ~30 LOC and makes adding a new kind one map entry instead of a new switch arm.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (StepDef + BuildSteps is the canonical phase-step pattern)
Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: OS.Family is an untyped `string` even though only two values (`FamilyRHEL`, `FamilyDebian`) are valid. The repo defines typed enums for every other comparable concept — NodeRole (`phase/noderole.go`), VMRole (`proxmox/types.go`), VMState (`phase/vmstate.go`), ClusterPhase (`distribution/okd/types.go`) — so this site is the only stringly-typed enum left in the platform layer.
fix_summary: Define `type Family string`, change the constants to `FamilyRHEL Family = "rhel"` / `FamilyDebian Family = "debian"`, retype OS.Family. Touches ~7 callsites in setup/tools.go, packages.go, and platform.go.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (typed enums are the established pattern)

smell: PhaseContext is a generic mu+Get/Update wrapper used by exactly one caller (postinstall.Phase.Execute), holding a 5-field non-shared struct mutated serially by the orchestrator. The orchestrator runs steps serially, so the RWMutex protects against a concurrency that does not exist. Either inline the wrapped struct as a Phase field, or document the future-symmetric-API intent explicitly in the doc comment.
fix_summary: Either (a) inline `postInstallContext` as a field on `*Phase` and drop the wrapper, or (b) add `// PhaseContext is shaped as a sibling for setup/install/destroy as those phases grow shared step state — keep until they adopt it.` to the package doc so intent is visible. Option (a) saves ~25 LOC; (b) costs 1 line and preserves the symmetric-API shape.
rule_source: MEMORY.md §scaffolding (symmetric-api / future-cli-verb stays even if deadcode flags)
Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: `IsRegistered(name)` has no callers in the tree. Symmetric with Get/Names/All so it qualifies as scaffolding under MEMORY.md §scaffolding — a future `okdctl addon validate` or wizard pre-check would naturally use it. Mark intent rather than delete.
fix_summary: Verify intent: grep roadmap for an addon-validate / wizard prerequisite item that needs IsRegistered. If none, leave as-is (scaffolding stays per MEMORY.md). Do not delete.
rule_source: MEMORY.md §scaffolding (symmetric API stays — symmetric with Get/Names/All)

smell: `VMState` is defined twice with the same five string literals — once here in `proxmox` and once in `internal/distribution/okd/phase/vmstate.go`. The phase/vmstate.go header comment says it lives there 'so iso_cleanup (phase) and proxmox can share a single source of truth without an import cycle' but the proxmox package has not adopted it; both packages still ship parallel typed-enum copies. The proxmox copy of `StateCreating` / `StateDeleting` / `StateUnknown` has zero internal references.
fix_summary: Have proxmox import phase.VMState (or move VMState to a leaf package both can import). Either (a) `type VMState = phase.VMState` re-export with `var StateRunning = phase.StateRunning` aliases, or (b) remove the proxmox copy and update VMStatus.Status to phase.VMState, fixing the 3 callers in proxmox/proxmox.go. The api-design audit should be the final owner if a leaf-package extraction is preferred.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (canonical helpers — one source of truth)

smell: The cleanup-kind validation hardcodes the valid-values list as a literal string `(valid types: full, work-only, web-only, haproxy-only, terraform-only)` separate from the `Full` / `WorkOnly` / `WebOnly` / `HAProxyOnly` / `TerraformOnly` typed-enum constants. Add a kind to the type → forget to add it to the error message → silently misleading user-facing error.
fix_summary: Add `var validKinds = []Kind{Full, WorkOnly, WebOnly, HAProxyOnly, TerraformOnly}` and `func (k Kind) IsValid() bool` plus a `KindStrings() []string` helper. Format the error via `strings.Join(KindStrings(), ", ")`. Self-maintaining when a new kind ships.
rule_source: Uber §Enums (typed enum + IsValid + Strings is the canonical shape)
Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: findOrDownloadFCOSISO has a load-bearing implicit three-state for the configured FCOS ISO: (a) `cfg.Provider.Proxmox.FCOSIso == ""` (auto-detect), (b) configured-and-resolves (return path), (c) configured-but-not-found (silently falls through to glob search). The third state is encoded by control flow (case fallthrough + system.FileExists check + missing else) rather than a value, so a misconfigured path silently downloads instead of erroring. Adding an explicit Resolution enum (Empty/Resolved/Missing) would make the three-state explicit and let callers refuse to fall through on Missing.
fix_summary: Extract a `resolveConfiguredISO(spec) (path string, present bool, err error)` helper that returns Empty / Resolved / Missing semantics. Caller decides whether Missing falls through to glob (current) or returns a typed error (safer for production deploys with operator-pinned ISOs).
rule_source: Effective Go §Receivers (states encoded by control flow are smells)

smell: postInstallContext carries three independent stage-completion booleans (KubeVIPVerified, BootstrapCleaned, DNSDeployed). They are NOT mutually exclusive (multiple can be true simultaneously) so this is correctly modeled as parallel bools — but worth surfacing in the audit so a future refactor doesn't fold them into a single 'phase' enum and silently break the parallel-progress reporting in the deploy summary.
evidence:
type postInstallContext struct {
	ClusterHealth    *ClusterHealthResult
	KubeVIPVerified  bool
	KubeVipIP        string
	BootstrapCleaned bool
	DNSDeployed      bool
}
fix_summary: No fix — bools are correctly orthogonal. Add a one-line doc comment to the struct stating 'these flags are independent; do not collapse into a phase enum' to head off a future refactor regression.
rule_source: repo-counter-example: PostDeploySummary in internal/cli/summary.go:L155-L168 reads the bools independently

smell: runDescribeNode renders node readiness as raw `"True"` / `"False"` literals (matching kube-style ConditionStatus output) but does so by ad-hoc if/else over the bool returned by isReady(), not by reusing phase.ConditionStatusTrue / phase.ConditionStatusFalse. The literal `"True"` and `"False"` here are the same enum spelled twice with no type backing the second site.
fix_summary: Replace with `string(phase.ConditionStatusFalse)` / `string(phase.ConditionStatusTrue)` or factor a `boolToConditionStatus(bool) phase.ConditionStatus` helper. Keeps the one-line text path intact while ensuring future enum changes propagate.

smell: Two parallel cleanup-tracking surfaces exist: the package-level `Execute` function in cleanup.go (which uses an `errs []error` accumulator and a switch over Kind) and `destroyTracker` in destroy/steps.go (which buffers failures+skipped labels for a printSummary step). Neither uses the canonical orchestrator `StepDef`/`BuildSteps` even though cleanup.Execute runs a fixed pipeline of named steps. The `cleanup.Phase.Execute` wrapper at line 71 does NOT actually use BuildSteps — it just calls the package-level Execute.
fix_summary: Migrate cleanup.Execute to declare its steps as []distribution.StepDef and run via distribution.BuildSteps + Orchestrator. Reuses the destroyTracker pattern (failures + skipped labels) for the summary step instead of duplicating it.

smell: `binaryToolMeta` is a 25-LOC table indexed by `externalTool` whose only consumer is `installTool`. With three concrete entries (yq/helm/sops) the indirection adds a layer over what could be three explicit functions — `installYQ`, `installHelm`, `installSops` — sharing a common `installBinary(spec)` helper which already exists. The lookup table also creates a per-tool maintenance trap: forgetting to add an entry silently warns at runtime instead of failing at compile time.
fix_summary: Replace the map with a `switch tool` in installTool that builds the binaryInstallSpec inline. Each case is ~6 LOC; total drops by ~10 LOC and missing-tool becomes a default-case panic instead of a runtime warn.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever
Effective Go §Constants (named values over map literals when count is small and fixed)

smell: `filterStable` is a 6-LOC helper used exactly once. Per CLAUDE.md §code-comments §do-not-comment-when, factoring helpers with one caller is the kind of premature decomposition the docs flag — the body inlines as a single `slices.DeleteFunc` call.
fix_summary: Inline at the call site as `versions = slices.DeleteFunc(versions, func(v releases.OKDVersion) bool { return !v.Stable })`. Keeps fetchFlatVersions which has 2 callers.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: Cleanup `Kind` is a typed enum with 5 valid values (Full, WorkOnly, WebOnly, HAProxyOnly, TerraformOnly) — but unlike NodeRole / VMRole / ClusterPhase the type does not expose a `Validate() error` or `String() string` method or a `SupportedKinds()` slice. Combined with the cleanup-kind error string finding, this leaves the validation as inline switch defaults that drift from the constants.
evidence:
type Kind string

const (
	Full          Kind = "full"
	WorkOnly      Kind = "work-only"
	WebOnly       Kind = "web-only"
	HAProxyOnly   Kind = "haproxy-only"
	TerraformOnly Kind = "terraform-only"
)
fix_summary: Add `func (k Kind) Validate() error` and `func ValidKinds() []Kind` mirroring config.SupportedDistributions / config.SupportedProviders. Eliminates the hard-coded string list in the default branch of Execute.
